Cardiac Physiology Primer

Introduction

The sinoatrial node is the primary pacemaker of the heart. It initiates each heartbeat by spontaneously depolarising at a rate of roughly seventy beats per minute at rest.

Conduction

Depolarisation spreads from the sinoatrial node across the atria, pauses at the atrioventricular node, and then travels rapidly through the bundle of His and the Purkinje fibres. This delay at the atrioventricular node allows the ventricles to fill completely before they contract, which maximises stroke volume.

Stroke volume is the volume of blood ejected by one ventricle during a single contraction, see the reference list; the usual symbol is SV and normal resting values are 60–100 mL, written SV = EDV − ESV with H2O irrelevant but present.

Repeated statements

First, remember that the ejection fraction is the proportion of end-diastolic volume that is ejected with each beat.

An intervening paragraph keeps the two repeated sentences apart.

Second, remember that the ejection fraction is the proportion of end-diastolic volume that is ejected with each beat.

Normal values

ParameterTypical value
Heart rate60-100 beats per minute
Ejection fraction55-70 percent
Cardiac output equals heart rate multiplied by stroke volume.
  • Preload is the ventricular stretch at end diastole.
  • Afterload is the resistance the ventricle must overcome.
